questions.stem: A gym charges a fixed membership fee plus a constant fee per training session. Membership with 2 sessions costs $125; membership with 5 sessions costs $260. What is the greatest number of sessions that can be purchased with membership for at most $370?
questions.explanation: Три дополнительные тренировки стоят 135, значит одна — 45 долларов. Членство стоит 125−2·45=35. Неравенство 35+45n≤370 даёт n≤7,44; целое максимальное n=7. Нельзя округлять вверх.

questions.stem: A school had 1,001 students in 2004 and 1,697 in 2008. A linear model gives the enrollment at the start of each calendar year. According to the model, what is the first integer year with enrollment at least 2,400?
questions.explanation: Рост 696 за 4 года, то есть 174 в год. 1001+174(y−2004)≥2400 ⇒ y≥2012,04. Первый целый год 2013; в 2012 прогноз 2393.

questions.explanation: За 8 лет прибавилось 1520, по 190 в год. От 1999 до 2003 ещё 4 года: 5880+4·190=6640.

questions.stem: For a real constant k, the system (k−1)x+3y=8 and 4x+(k+1)y=6 has no solution. What is the sum of the squares of all possible values of k?
questions.explanation: Определитель равен (k−1)(k+1)−12=k²−13. Особые значения ±√13. Совместность потребовала бы коэффициент пропорции 6/8=3/4 и 4/(k−1)=3/4, то есть k=19/3, что не является особым значением. Поэтому оба ±√13 дают отсутствие решений; сумма квадратов 26.

questions.explanation: За час заполнено 1/6+1/4=5/12 бака. Осталось 7/12; со скоростью 1/6 бака в час требуется (7/12)/(1/6)=3,5 дополнительных часа. 4,5 — полное время, а не дополнительное.

questions.explanation: Подставляем y−5=2x: x²+4x²=9, значит x²=9/5. Первая четверть выбирает положительный x; квадрат уже определён. Использовать y вместо y−5 было бы ошибкой.

questions.stem: A square is inscribed in a circle of radius 5. A second circle is inscribed in that square. What fraction of the area of the first circle is the area of the second circle?
questions.explanation: Диагональ квадрата 10, его сторона 5√2. Радиус внутренней окружности — половина стороны: 5/√2. Отношение площадей равно отношению квадратов радиусов: (25/2)/25=1/2.

questions.stem: A cone has height 12 cm and base radius 8 cm, with its vertex downward. Water initially reaches 6 cm above the vertex and is then added until it reaches 9 cm. What fraction of the cone's total volume was added?
questions.explanation: Для подобных конусов объёмная доля — куб отношения высот. Первоначально (6/12)³=1/8=8/64, затем (9/12)³=27/64. Добавили 27/64−8/64=19/64 полного объёма.

questions.stem: A tower is 400 feet horizontally from a window. From the window, the angle of elevation to the tower's top is 36° and the angle of depression to its base is 23°. What is the tower's height, in feet, to the nearest tenth?
questions.explanation: Высота выше окна 400·tan36°, ниже окна 400·tan23°. Складываем: 400(tan36°+tan23°)≈460,407. До десятых 460,4. Только один угол учитывал бы лишь часть башни.

questions.passage: After reading a letter that challenges her view of two acquaintances, Elizabeth Bennet does more than exchange one favorable judgment for another. She recognizes that she welcomed the man who flattered her and distrusted the one who wounded her pride. She had regarded these reactions as evidence of exceptional discernment. Now the very confidence with which she judged others becomes part of what she must examine. Her admission that she had not known herself follows her acknowledgment that vanity encouraged her to seek confirmation rather than to weigh evidence impartially.
questions.stem: Which inference about Elizabeth's revised judgment is best supported?
choices: It involves questioning the motives that made her earlier judgments seem reliable.
It replaces an unfavorable judgment with a favorable one while leaving her confidence in her judging method intact.
It shows that a judgment influenced by vanity must reach a factually incorrect conclusion in every instance.
It depends on determining whether the flattering acquaintance intended to deceive her.
questions.explanation:
A — верно: Она проверяет не только сведения о знакомых, но и собственную заинтересованность, которую раньше принимала за проницательность.

B — неверно: Подмена оценки людей недостаточна: Элизабет ставит под вопрос сам способ суждения.

C — неверно: Выявленный риск пристрастности не доказывает ложность каждого отдельного прежнего вывода.

D — неверно: Рассуждение касается влияния лести на Элизабет, а не необходимости установить чужой умысел.

questions.passage: Mary Bennet observes that pride and vanity are often treated as interchangeable. She nevertheless distinguishes them by the object of a person's concern. Pride, she says, relates chiefly to the opinion people hold of themselves; vanity concerns the opinion they want others to hold of them. On her account, a person might have a high estimate of personal worth without making the admiration of other people an essential goal. The two dispositions can coexist, but the presence of one does not by itself establish the presence of the other.
questions.stem: Which statement best captures Mary's distinction?
choices: Pride is always imaginary, whereas vanity is based on genuine achievement.
A favorable self-opinion does not necessarily entail a desire for others' admiration.
Anyone who seeks admiration must have a low opinion of personal worth.
The words differ only in politeness and describe exactly the same concern.
questions.explanation:
A — неверно: Мэри не связывает различие с подлинностью достижений.

B — верно: Различаются мнение о себе и желаемое мнение окружающих; первое не обязательно влечёт второе.

C — неверно: Такой обратной зависимости текст не устанавливает.

D — неверно: Это отрицает содержательное различие, которое она проводит.

questions.passage: Darcy explains that he once interfered in his friend's attachment because he believed the woman did not return it. Later, he tells his friend that this interpretation was mistaken. He also admits that he had concealed information relevant to the relationship. The friend's attachment, Darcy observes, has not diminished. Darcy therefore expects happiness from a renewed courtship. His changed expectation follows the correction of his own account of the woman's feelings, rather than a claim that his friend's feelings have suddenly become stronger.
questions.stem: Which finding would most directly undermine the reasoning behind Darcy's new expectation?
choices: His friend had cared for the woman before Darcy changed his advice.
Darcy admits that his previous interference was inappropriate.
Reliable evidence shows that the woman remains indifferent to his friend.
Some information was withheld during the earlier courtship.
questions.explanation:
A — неверно: Это прямо согласуется с тем, что чувство не ослабло.

B — неверно: Признание ошибки уже входит в новый рассказ, а не опровергает его.

C — верно: Прогноз опирается на исправленное представление о взаимности; доказанное равнодушие разрушало бы именно эту опору.

D — неверно: Сокрытие объясняет прежнюю ошибку и не доказывает неверность новой оценки.

questions.passage: Watson has used the staircase to Holmes's rooms many times, yet he cannot say how many steps it contains. Holmes can give the number: seventeen. For Holmes, the contrast illustrates a distinction between encountering something repeatedly and attending to its features. Watson has certainly looked at the stairs; Holmes does not accuse him of having failed to use his eyes. Instead, the detective treats the absence of a particular piece of knowledge as evidence that repeated visual exposure need not amount to deliberate observation.
questions.stem: Which conclusion follows most directly from Holmes's example?
choices: A person who cannot count the steps must be unable to recognize the staircase.
Holmes's count proves that only detectives can learn from ordinary surroundings.
The greater a person's familiarity, the less accurate every observation becomes.
Frequent exposure can coexist with failure to register a specific observable detail.
questions.explanation:
A — неверно: Незнание числа не означает неспособности узнавать лестницу.

B — неверно: Профессиональная исключительность из примера не следует.

C — неверно: Текст допускает отсутствие одного знания, а не всеобщее ухудшение с опытом.

D — верно: Уотсон видел лестницу много раз, но не выделял число ступеней как объект внимания.

questions.passage: Holmes warns that constructing a theory before collecting evidence can alter the direction of an inquiry. Once attached to a theory, an investigator may begin to reinterpret observations so that they support it, instead of allowing observations to test it. The warning does not require investigators to work without any expectations. It concerns a tendency to protect a favored explanation by making the evidence conform to it, particularly when contrary details would otherwise prompt revision.
questions.stem: Which investigator's behavior most clearly illustrates the risk Holmes describes?
choices: An investigator treats confirming details as reliable but dismisses comparable contrary details solely because they conflict with the preferred theory.
An investigator uses a provisional explanation to choose the next test while retaining results that could count against the explanation.
An investigator discounts a contrary measurement after independent calibration shows that the instrument was unreliable.
An investigator reinterprets an ambiguous record after newly obtained independent evidence challenges the initial interpretation.
questions.explanation:
A — верно: Одинаковые по качеству данные оцениваются по совпадению с любимой теорией; это и есть подгонка.

B — неверно: Теория направляет проверку, но не защищается от опровержения: именно этого отличия требует оговорка текста.

C — неверно: Основание для исключения — независимо установленное качество измерения, а не само противоречие любимой теории.

D — неверно: Трактовка меняется под воздействием новых данных, а не ради сохранения первоначальной теории.

questions.passage: Darwin addresses the objection that gradual changes should have left more intermediate forms in the fossil record. He argues that the record is not a continuous inventory of everything that lived. Preservation requires particular circumstances, and the deposits available for study represent only portions of past environments and time. On this account, a gap between known forms could reflect a gap in preservation or discovery. This response does not identify a fossil for every predicted transition; it challenges the assumption that failure to find one is equivalent to proof that none existed.
questions.stem: Which conclusion is most consistent with the passage?
choices: A preservation gap is positive evidence that any particular predicted intermediate form actually existed.
The evidential force of an absence depends partly on how complete the relevant record can reasonably be expected to be.
The incompleteness of a record makes all competing explanations equally well supported by whatever fossils are available.
Once a later form is abundant in a collection, the absence of its predicted predecessors establishes that they never existed.
questions.explanation:
A — неверно: Ослабление отрицательного довода не превращается в положительное подтверждение каждой предполагаемой формы.

B — верно: Аргумент связывает значение отсутствия находок с неполнотой сохранения и обнаружения.

C — неверно: Неполнота не отменяет возможность сравнивать объяснения по существующим данным.

D — неверно: Обилие более поздней формы не доказывает сопоставимость условий сохранения разных периодов.

questions.passage: Darwin uses red clover to illustrate how the abundance of one organism may depend on several others. Bumblebees visit the flowers and help produce seed. Field mice can destroy bumblebee nests, while cats can reduce the numbers of those mice. A connection between cats and clover would therefore be indirect, passing through the other organisms. The example is intended to show why an organism's success cannot always be explained by examining only its immediate competitors or the climate around it.
questions.stem: Which finding would most directly support the particular indirect relationship described?
choices: Cats eat clover leaves more often than mice do.
Clover grows in some places without cats.
Where cats reduce nest-destroying mice, more bumblebee nests survive and clover seed production increases.
Rainfall increases at the same time in every observed field.
questions.explanation:
A — неверно: Предложенный механизм не связан с поеданием листьев кошками.

B — неверно: Возможность роста без кошек не проверяет изменение по указанной цепи.

C — верно: Находка проверяет последовательность всех звеньев: кошки → мыши → гнёзда шмелей → семена клевера.

D — неверно: Общий климатический сдвиг не выделяет механизм через мышей и шмелей.

questions.passage: In discussing domestic animals, Darwin separates the appearance of variation from a breeder's use of it. A breeder can preserve and combine differences already present among individuals, favoring those that serve a chosen purpose. The remarkable differences between established breeds may thus result from many acts of selection, even when the individual differences available at any one time were modest. The account assigns an important role to human choice without implying that a breeder can simply call a desired hereditary difference into existence.
questions.stem: Which claim would go beyond what the passage supports?
choices: Selection over many generations can accumulate initially modest differences.
Human preferences can affect which variants are retained in a domestic population.
The origin of a variant and its subsequent preservation are distinguishable processes.
A breeder's desire for a trait is sufficient to make that hereditary trait appear.
questions.explanation:
A — неверно: Это прямо соответствует объяснению накопления изменений.

B — неверно: Благоприятствование нужным вариантам — описанная роль выбора.

C — неверно: Это исходное различие, на котором построен текст.

D — верно: Это неподдержанный переход от отбора имеющихся различий к созданию признака одним желанием.

questions.passage: Darwin argues that a natural classification should reflect relationships of descent. A feature can be highly useful for an animal's present way of life without being especially informative about its ancestry. Conversely, a seemingly unimportant feature may be valuable for classification if it has been inherited from a common ancestor. Similar habits can produce resemblances in animals that are not closely related. Classifying organisms solely by their present occupations would therefore risk treating an adaptive resemblance as if it established a shared genealogical history.
questions.stem: Which observation would most clearly illustrate the distinction?
choices: Two distantly related animals have similar swimming structures, while a less conspicuous inherited feature links one of them to its close relatives.
Two animals are grouped together because their similarly useful structures are conspicuous, even though no evidence about ancestry is considered.
An investigator removes all useful structures from a classification, assuming that usefulness always rules out inheritance from a common ancestor.
An investigator treats a minor resemblance as proof of close ancestry solely because it has no known present function.
questions.explanation:
A — верно: Вариант противопоставляет сходство по функции и признак происхождения — оба элемента рассуждения.

B — неверно: Такой подход иллюстрирует риск, который текст критикует, но не правильное различение функции и происхождения.

C — неверно: Отсутствие гарантии информативности не означает несовместимости полезности с наследованием.

D — неверно: Малозаметность и отсутствие известной функции сами по себе ещё не доказывают общее происхождение.

questions.passage: Douglass recalls that the woman who began teaching him to read did not immediately become an opponent of his education. He describes her later refusal to teach, and her efforts to prevent others from teaching him, as changes connected with exercising power over another person. His account grants that her early kindness was real. It also insists that this kindness did not protect her from adopting the practices of the slaveholding system. The chronology matters because it presents her conduct as something that developed, rather than as an unchanging disposition visible from the beginning.
questions.stem: What does the sequence of events chiefly support?
choices: The early instruction was secretly intended to make later instruction impossible.
Participation in an oppressive system can reshape a person's conduct despite earlier kindness.
Douglass believed education could occur only under a regular teacher.
Her behavior remained identical throughout the period he describes.
questions.explanation:
A — неверно: Раннюю доброту текст признаёт подлинной; скрытый план не указан.

B — верно: Аргумент опирается на изменение от помощи к пресечению учёбы под влиянием власти.

C — неверно: Его дальнейшее обучение как раз обходилось без постоянного учителя.

D — неверно: Это отменяет смысл показанной хронологии.

questions.passage: When regular instruction was denied him, Douglass found opportunities to learn from boys he met during errands. He sometimes carried bread, which he could offer to boys who had less to eat. In return, they helped him learn to read. The exchange linked two different forms of need: the boys' immediate hunger and his need for access to written language. Describing what he received as more valuable, Douglass does not deny the usefulness of bread. He emphasizes the lasting importance of the knowledge that the arrangement enabled him to acquire.
questions.stem: Which interpretation of the exchange is best supported?
choices: The boys refused food because reading had no practical value to them.
Douglass considered physical hunger imaginary rather than important.
Something he could supply for an immediate need helped him gain knowledge he valued for its lasting consequences.
The arrangement depended on a formal school accepting him as a student.
questions.explanation:
A — неверно: Текст описывает обмен, а не отказ от хлеба.

B — неверно: Сравнение ценности не отрицает реальности и важности голода.

C — верно: Хлеб удовлетворяет непосредственный голод, а ответный урок даёт долго сохраняющееся знание.

D — неверно: Обмен происходил во время поручений, вне регулярного обучения.

questions.passage: Alice sharply tells herself to stop crying. The narrator remarks that she generally gives herself good advice but seldom follows it. Alice sometimes scolds herself so severely that she brings tears to her own eyes. The account even recalls her attempt to punish herself for cheating in a game she was playing against herself. These details present a child capable of taking several roles in an imagined dispute, without suggesting that her ability to formulate a sensible rule guarantees that she will act on it.
questions.stem: Which detail most directly supports the idea that knowing a rule does not ensure acting on it?
choices: Alice is able to imagine taking more than one role.
The narrator recalls an earlier game.
A rule can be expressed in a complete sentence.
Alice usually gives herself good advice but rarely follows it.
questions.explanation:
A — неверно: Способность разыгрывать роли сама по себе не показывает разрыв знания и действия.

B — неверно: Само наличие воспоминания не является нужным свидетельством.

C — неверно: Такое утверждение в тексте вообще не обсуждается.

D — верно: В этой детали прямо сопоставлены верный совет и его невыполнение.

questions.passage: Mary distinguishes pride from vanity while the narrator notes that she prides herself on the solidity of her reflections. Mary explains that pride concerns one's own estimate of oneself, whereas vanity concerns the estimate one wishes others to make. The narrator's description does not formally disprove Mary's distinction. It places the speaker inside the territory she is discussing, however: her satisfaction in the depth of her own thought becomes visible at the very moment she offers a confident general account of self-regard.
questions.stem: What is the main effect of the narrator's description of Mary?
choices: It introduces an ironic relation between Mary's analysis and her own evident self-regard.
It supplies independent evidence that Mary's conceptual distinction is invalid, rather than commenting on her relation to the subject.
It presents Mary's satisfaction in her reasoning as evidence that she is chiefly seeking an audience's admiration.
It endorses Mary's self-estimate as an objective measure of the quality of her reflections.
questions.explanation:
A — верно: Мэри объясняет самодовольство, а ремарка показывает его у неё самой; различие терминов при этом не опровергнуто.

questions.passage: When Holmes returns disguised as a clergyman, Watson notices more than a change of clothes. The detective's expression, manner, and apparent disposition have changed with the role. Watson comments that the stage lost a fine actor when Holmes became a specialist in crime, just as science lost an acute reasoner. The remark praises abilities visible in Holmes's chosen work by imagining what those same abilities could have contributed to occupations he did not pursue.
questions.stem: Which choice best describes the function of Watson's reference to the stage and science?
choices: It reports that Holmes had already held permanent jobs in both fields.
It conveys the range of Holmes's talents by imagining alternative careers that could have used them.
It argues that his disguise fails because his costume is too theatrical.
It denies that acting and reasoning are relevant to detective work.
questions.explanation:

questions.passage: Alice wonders whether she has changed during the night. Yesterday everything seemed ordinary, but now her experiences no longer fit what she expects. She tries to recall whether she felt the same on waking, then asks who she is if she is no longer the same person. She begins considering other children she knows, as though a change in her circumstances might mean that she has become one of them. Her attempt to explain the strange world therefore becomes a question about the continuity of her own identity.
questions.stem: How does the passage develop Alice's concern?
choices: It moves from certainty about a scientific result to a formal proof.
It lists the names of every child Alice has ever met.
It moves from unexpected experiences to an effort to determine whether she herself has changed.
It explains that Alice has already identified which child she has become.
questions.explanation:
A — неверно: Ни научной уверенности, ни доказательства в тексте нет.

B — неверно: Она думает о знакомых детях, но полного списка текст не даёт.

C — верно: Сначала необычен мир, затем Алиса переносит вопрос на собственную личность.

questions.passage: The Mock Turtle describes a school where the hours of instruction became fewer each day: ten on the first day, nine on the next, and so on. When Alice asks about this arrangement, the explanation plays on the sound of the word lessons and the verb lessen. An ordinary term for periods of instruction is treated as if its sound provided a rule for organizing the school day. The exchange uses a resemblance between words to make a familiar institution behave according to an unfamiliar logic.
questions.stem: As used in the passage, lessen most nearly means
choices: teach
remember
continue
decrease

A — неверно: Уроки связаны с преподаванием, но lessen означает не это.

B — неверно: Воспоминание не объясняет сокращение часов.

C — неверно: Продолжение не передаёт изменение количества вниз.

questions.passage: Darwin explains that he uses struggle for existence in a broad, metaphorical sense. Two animals competing for food fit the phrase, but so does a plant's dependence on moisture or on another organism that helps it reproduce. The term includes success in leaving offspring, not merely survival through a direct physical contest. By setting out this broad usage, Darwin prepares readers to recognize pressures and dependencies that would disappear from view if struggle were understood only as an encounter between fighting individuals.
questions.stem: Why does the passage emphasize that Darwin's use of struggle is metaphorical?
choices: To prevent readers from limiting the concept to direct physical conflict.
To withdraw the claim that organisms depend on resources.
To claim that reproduction has no role in the argument.
To separate all plants from the discussion of existence.
questions.explanation:
A — верно: Уточнение расширяет смысл до зависимостей и воспроизводства.

B — неверно: Зависимость от ресурсов приводится как пример, а не отвергается.

C — неверно: Продолжение рода прямо включено в смысл термина.

D — неверно: Растения служат важным примером широкого употребления.

questions.passage: Darwin compares the relationships of organisms to a tree whose growing branches represent forms now living. The branches diverge from older limbs, and many earlier branches have ceased to grow. On this picture, living forms need not stand in a single sequence from least to most advanced. Their relations depend on branching histories, some represented by surviving offshoots and others interrupted by extinction. The image combines present diversity with the loss of forms that once connected parts of that diversity more visibly.
questions.stem: Which feature of the analogy most directly represents the effect of extinction on present diversity?
choices: Every living branch occupies the same position along a single unbranched trunk.
Some earlier branches no longer grow, although surviving offshoots remain part of the tree.
The tree has no historical connection between its limbs.
A larger leaf necessarily represents a morally superior organism.
questions.explanation:
A — неверно: Такое устройство уничтожает главное свойство образа — ветвление.

B — верно: Прервавшиеся ветви передают исчезновение форм при сохранении других линий общего дерева.

C — неверно: Образ как раз представляет исторические связи.

D — неверно: Размер и моральная оценка не входят в аналогию.

questions.passage: Douglass describes reading as giving shape and language to his opposition to enslavement. Yet the knowledge it brought could also deepen his unhappiness: he understood his condition more fully without immediately gaining the means to escape it. These responses are presented together, rather than as evidence that one of them was insincere. His account distinguishes a change in understanding from a change in material freedom, showing how the first could be transformative even while the second remained out of reach.
questions.stem: What is the function of describing reading as both empowering and painful?
choices: To concede that reading produced no meaningful change until a practical means of escape became available.
To imply that improved understanding normally supplies the material freedom whose absence had caused the distress.
To distinguish the expansion of understanding from the immediate ability to change one's circumstances.
To rank emotional comfort as a more reliable measure of educational value than increased understanding.
questions.explanation:
A — неверно: Понимание уже названо преобразующим, хотя немедленного выхода из несвободы ещё нет.

B — неверно: Рассуждение разводит эти два изменения, а не устанавливает автоматический переход между ними.

C — верно: Знание даёт осмысление и язык сопротивления, но ещё не обеспечивает возможности побега; отсюда обе реакции.

D — неверно: Текст показывает совместимость боли и ценности знания, а не делает комфорт критерием его пользы.

questions.passage: Darwin distinguishes deliberate breeding toward a specified standard from a process he calls unconscious selection. People may repeatedly preserve the animals they find most useful or attractive without intending to create a new breed. Over generations, their choices can nevertheless change the population. In this usage, unconscious does not mean that the people are asleep or unaware of which animal they keep. It concerns the absence of an explicit long-term project corresponding to the accumulated result.
questions.stem: As used in the passage, unconscious most nearly means
choices: performed only while asleep
incapable of producing any lasting change
governed by a complete written breeding standard
not directed toward a consciously planned long-term result
questions.explanation:
A — неверно: Здесь нет буквального сна или потери сознания.

B — неверно: Накопительные изменения прямо описаны.

C — неверно: Это соответствовало бы намеренному отбору, с которым проводится различие.

D — верно: Люди выбирают животных осознанно, но не ставят конечную цель вывести новую породу.

questions.passage: Elizabeth contrasts her sister Jane's readiness to think well of others with her own habit of quickly finding faults. Jane is reluctant to assume bad motives when a more generous interpretation is available. Elizabeth sometimes regards this candour as excessive, yet later recognizes that her own critical judgments have also been shaped by vanity. In this context, the sister's candour concerns the charitable way she interprets other people, rather than an eagerness to voice every unfavorable thought without restraint.
questions.stem: As used in the passage, candour most nearly means
choices: generosity in judging others
financial generosity through gifts
harsh frankness in expressing criticism
certainty based on complete knowledge
questions.explanation:
A — верно: Контекст определяет благожелательное толкование чужих мотивов, а не резкую откровенность.

B — неверно: Речь о суждениях, а не о денежных подарках.

C — неверно: Это противоречит нежеланию Джейн приписывать дурные мотивы.

D — неверно: Благожелательность не означает полного знания фактов.

questions.passage: A man describes to Holmes an organization that offers paid employment only to men with a particular hair color. The work consists of copying entries from an encyclopedia, and the conditions for keeping the position seem unrelated to the value of the copying itself. Holmes treats the arrangement as singular. What interests him is not merely that one person accepted the position, but that several details of the offer are sufficiently unusual to suggest that its stated purpose may not be its actual purpose.

unusual
widely accepted as ordinary
incapable of investigation

B — верно: Особенность предложения, а не грамматическое число или одиночество человека, привлекает внимание.

C — неверно: Напротив, условия выглядят необычными.

questions.passage:
Text 1
A breeder repeatedly keeps individuals possessing a favored difference. After many generations, the population may exhibit that difference more strongly. The breeder's purpose helps determine which variations are preserved.

Text 2
In nature, differences that improve an organism's success under existing conditions can be preserved through differential survival and reproduction. No breeder needs to foresee the eventual result. The conditions under which organisms live affect which differences prove advantageous.
questions.stem: Which statement best describes a relationship between the texts?
choices: Text 2 transfers the breeder's deliberate planning to the organisms themselves while retaining the same requirement for foresight.
Text 1 explains differences by their initial appearance, whereas Text 2 alone explains their preservation.
Both describe the preservation of variation over generations, while Text 2 removes the need for a chooser with a planned goal.
Text 2 treats the inheritance of a variation as sufficient to preserve it regardless of the conditions organisms face.
questions.explanation:
A — неверно: Отсутствие селекционера не означает переноса его сознательной цели на организмы.

B — неверно: Первый текст тоже описывает повторное сохранение различий, а не только их возникновение.

C — верно: Общий механизм — неодинаковое сохранение различий; различается наличие человеческой цели.

D — неверно: Второй текст связывает преимущество с условиями жизни; одной наследуемости недостаточно.

questions.passage:
Text 1
Mary distinguishes pride, an opinion of oneself, from vanity, a concern with what others think. A person may have the first without necessarily having the second.

Text 2
Elizabeth recognizes that being flattered by one acquaintance and slighted by another influenced judgments she had considered independent. Her favorable estimate of her own discernment had concealed how much she wanted those judgments to confirm a pleasing view of herself.
questions.stem: How does Text 2 relate to the distinction in Text 1?
choices: It supplies a counterexample to Text 1 by showing that pride and vanity sometimes occur together.
It illustrates pride without vanity because Elizabeth's conclusions concern her own discernment rather than anyone else's views of her.
It shows that concern with others' opinions necessarily eliminates a favorable opinion of oneself.
It presents a case where the two concerns interact without disproving that they can be distinguished.
questions.explanation:
A — неверно: Text 1 допускает различение, но не утверждает невозможности совместного присутствия.

B — неверно: Уверенность в проницательности связана с реакцией на лесть и пренебрежение: второй компонент нельзя удалить.

C — неверно: У Элизабет эти два компонента прежде поддерживали друг друга, а не взаимно исключались.

D — верно: У Элизабет мнение о себе и чувствительность к чужой оценке связаны; это не опровергает различимость понятий.

questions.passage:
While researching selection, a student takes these notes:
- Breeders can choose individuals possessing desired differences.
- Deliberate selection aims at an explicit breeding goal.
- Unconscious selection can arise when people keep useful animals without intending to create a new breed.
- Both processes can accumulate differences over generations.
- The distinction concerns intention, not whether inherited variation is involved.
questions.stem: The student wants to emphasize a similarity while preserving the distinction between the processes. Which choice best achieves this goal?
choices: Both deliberate and unconscious selection can accumulate inherited differences, although only the former requires an explicit breeding goal.
Only deliberate selection can change animals over generations.
Unconscious selection means that people never choose which animals to keep.
Breeders sometimes have explicit goals.
questions.explanation:
A — верно: Одновременно названы общая черта и критерий различия.

B — неверно: Это противоречит заметке о накоплении изменений в обоих процессах.

C — неверно: Выбор есть; отсутствует долгосрочная цель создания породы.

- Regular instruction was stopped.
- He continued looking for opportunities to learn.
- Boys he met during errands sometimes helped him read.
- Bread could be exchanged for instruction.
- Access to reading material also supported his learning.
- His education therefore involved several improvised methods rather than one continuous formal course.
questions.stem: Which choice best supports the generalization that Douglass adapted his learning methods to obstacles?
choices: Douglass received uninterrupted formal instruction from a single teacher.
After regular lessons ended, Douglass sought informal instruction during errands and used available resources to obtain it.
Bread is a kind of food that can be carried during errands.
Learning is possible only when a school provides a complete course.
questions.explanation:
A — неверно: Это противоречит прекращению регулярных уроков.

B — верно: Связаны препятствие, перемена способа и доступные средства.

C — неверно: Бытовая деталь не объясняет адаптацию обучения.

A student notes the Bennet family's responses to a ball:
- Mrs. Bennet is pleased by the admiration shown to Jane.
- Jane is pleased too, though less demonstratively.
- Elizabeth shares Jane's pleasure.
- Mary values being praised as accomplished.
- Catherine and Lydia value having dance partners.
- The family returns in good spirits, but the narrator assigns different immediate reasons to different members.
questions.stem: Which choice best expresses the contrast between the family's shared mood and its varied sources?
choices: Every Bennet family member is cheerful exclusively because Jane has been admired.
Their different interests prevent any shared positive response to the evening.
The family returns cheerful, although individual members find satisfaction in different kinds of attention and enjoyment.
Mary's pleasure demonstrates that no one else receives attention.

A — неверно: Общая причина ошибочно подменяет разные перечисленные мотивы.

B — неверно: Различия сочетаются с общим хорошим настроением.

C — верно: Сохранён общий результат и различие причин; ни одна из частных мотиваций не объявлена всеобщей.
